title: Feds share video of UAP that was captured by law enforcement in Colorado
excerpt: On September 18, the United States' Department of War released a sixth tranche of records related to declassifying unidentified aerial phenomenon (UAP) reports and once again, a report out of Colorado was among those featured. content:
OTC News

Published September 22, 2026 12:33pm

On September 18, the United States Department of War released a sixth tranche of records related to declassifying unidentified aerial phenomenon (UAP) reports and once again, a report out of Colorado was among those featured. While several Colorado UAP reports have been declassified already, this most recent release included video footage.

According to the Department of War, the person who reported the sighting was a local law enforcement officer in Colorado who spotted the UAP on October 1, 2023. Four clips of the sighting were published, with the officer describing the UAP as a “silent” phenomenon that had red, blue, and green flashing lights.

A brief transcript related to the sighting was also released, capturing the officer describing the scene. The officer says that the UAP was about 300 feet off the ground and orb-like, and while a location appears to be noted, that remains redacted. According to the officer, a check of the radar showed no aircraft flying in the area at the time the UAP was seen. The officer described the UAP as being stationary for about 15 minutes, then starting to fly closer to the officer. Unfortunately, that’s the extent of the transcript.

A 15-minute clip that was released does appear to capture the UAP while stationary, with the UAP appearing to move in other clips as well (example one, example two).

Viewers of the videos may notice that the bottom half is blurred at times. This was added by the All-Domain Anomaly Resolution Office in order to obscure information that could violate privacy concerns. It’s also worth noting that a cellular device was used to capture the clips with officials noting that the autofocus features and other automatic image-processing functions can lead to distortion when capturing distant subjects.

Those watching the clips that were published may be a bit disappointed that on the surface, they’re not too eventful. A dot in the sky that seems to be moving – and that’s about it. While that dot might not seem too significant, it does beg a question that could have some pretty significant implications – what did the officer actually see?
